title: Object-oriented versus procedural
context: What is the difference between object-oriented and procedural programming?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Procedural programming organises code as functions that operate on shared data. Object-oriented programming groups data and the operations on it into objects, and lets objects hide their state behind methods. OOP suits large systems that change often, because a change stays inside one class. Procedural code can be simpler and faster for small scripts or data transforms. Java is object-oriented, but it also supports functional style with lambdas and streams.

points.title: Data with behaviour
points.why: OOP keeps data and the code that changes it together, which limits side effects across the program.

points.title: Trade-off
points.why: OOP adds structure and indirection. For small or data-heavy tasks procedural code can be clearer.
